notes.title: Dev Talk: Development Update
notes.notes:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/EkYI74z.png[/img]

The [b]Rise of Avalon[/b] update went live on August 12, 2020, bringing the [b]Roads of Avalon[/b], [b]Corrupted Dungeons[/b], and much more to the world of Albion. In this Dev Talk, Game Director Robin Henkys gives an update about the current state of the game as well as a preview of what's coming next.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4QqL7GoYDVI
No time to watch, or prefer a written summary? Read on...
[h3]2020 in Albion[/h3]
2020 brought [b]two major updates[/b] and massive growth in player numbers. The last update was developed with [b]almost our entire team working from home[/b], and since then we’ve been busy dealing with the challenges of distributed production, increased player numbers, and staying on top of patches and future content.

Today we want to give you an update on what's coming next. [b]Two exciting developments[/b] are coming soon:

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/6bd1a0350ad1ace4274d9936c53891a208173bce.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Midseason Update: Brimstone & Mist[/h3]
The first of these is the [b]Brimstone & Mist Midseason Update[/b], which expands on the Rise of Avalon update launched this past summer:
[list]	[*][b]New Mobs and Traps in Corrupted Dungeons[/b], including Hellhounds, new Heretics and demons, deadly spike and lava traps, and an all-new final boss, the [b]Demonic Harbinger[/b][/*]	[*][b]Rebalanced existing mobs[/b] and [b]increased Demonic Shard health[/b] in Slayer difficulty[/*]	[*]Added numerous [b]fishing areas[/b] to Roads of Avalon[/*]	[*]Added an exclusive [b]rare fish[/b] that can only be caught in the Roads of Avalon, plus a new line of food and corresponding rare fish recipe[/*]	[*]Changes to [b]Disarray[/b] (zerg debuff):	[list]		[*]Disarray will now depend on [b]the relative difference in Disarray levels between you and your target[/b][/*]		[*]This will boost the importance of [b]damage dealers and healers[/b] while ensuring each role stays impactful no matter the size of the battle[/*]		[*]Disarray will still [b]protect smaller groups[/b] from being overwhelmed[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Changes to the [b]Smart Cluster Queue[/b]:	[list]		[*]Now keeps[b] existing parties together[/b] when possible[/*]		[*]Party leaders can now assign [b]party as well as player priorities[/b][/*]		[*]Improved the way the system deals with allied players, ensuring players don't displace allies[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]...and much more[/*][/list]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/5c6a3fb7a4e4eae07d9d67aedaa6c60c53eab94f.jpeg[/img]

Brimstone and Mist goes live on October 21 - read more about it [url=https://albiononline.com/en/news/brimstone-mist-arrives-october-21][b]here[/b][/url].
[h3]Android Updating + Google Play Open Beta[/h3][list]	[*]Improved [b]Android updating[/b]:	[list]		[*]I[b]n-app updating[/b] will [b]dramatically reduce the size[/b] of the .apk download[/*]		[*]Downloads [b]changed content only[/b], which should result in much faster patching[/*]		[*]Introduced with Brimstone and Mist, but will mostly affect [b]future patches[/b], since this update contains significant structural changes that need to be downloaded[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*][b]Google Play Store Beta:[/b]	[list]		[*]Happening in [b]early [/b][b]November[/b][/*]		[*]Install and update Albion Online via the [b]Google Play Store[/b], making it easy and convenient to keep the game updated[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list][h3]Looking to the Future[/h3]
Of course, the Midseason Update and the mobile version aren’t all we’ve been working on. With Rise of Avalon we concluded much of the work we set out to do in the Queen Update: we added [b]interconnectivity [/b]to the world, added a space for [b]mid-level guilds to play and live in[/b], and we added an [b]all-new solo activity[/b] with its own competitive metagame.

At this time, work has already begun on our next update, in which we finally want to fulfill our vision for a new and massively improved [b]Faction Warfare[/b] system. On top of that, we've got some exciting changes for [b]Hellgates[/b] planned as well. We'll be releasing more Dev Talks on these subjects after the release of Brimstone and Mist on October 21.

That's all for today - thanks for watching!

notes.title: Patch 5 Brings Black Market and Mobile Improvements
notes.notes:
Today's patch brings numerous fixes and quality-of-life improvements to gameplay in Albion. Here's a bit of what's new:

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/d0e8d2346aa1f918cb6a8893642235c7b67f4b92.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Black Market: Persistent Crafting Info and Improved Performance[/h3]
Items sold to the Black Market [b]will now retain their "crafted by" info[/b]. This means that a great deal of item loot from mobs and in treasure chests will now show who originally crafted the item. In addition to helping active crafters make a name for themselves, persistent item info adds to the depth and continuity of Albion's ever-changing world. This patch also includes performance improvements to Black Market item distribution, correcting an issue where "split" party loot mode would sometimes not work when looting items.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/96cdf2724eb1fc9dc03d959d79105c8b8710bb24.png[/img]
[h3]A Dynamic "Hotkey" and Other Mobile Improvements[/h3]
Starting with Patch 5, the mobile version includes [b]an additional "Custom Button" next to the spellbar[/b], with one fixed option ("Inspect") and four additional customizable buttons that can be set via the Settings menu. This button allows for everything from Autorun to party member selection to emotes, and is among the most-requested features for mobile devices. This button is still in the experimental stages, so give it a try and let us know your thoughts on our [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Board/138-Mobile-Version/][b]mobile forum[/b][/url].

Additional improvements include the ability to connect a mouse for desktop-style chat scrolling, the ability to send feedback and bug reports via a new UI, an "Increase Brightness" slider in Settings, and various bug fixes.
[h3]General Changes and Fixes[/h3][list]	[*]The health increase for Demonic Shards in Corrupted Dungeons that was intended for Patch 4 is now live.[/*]	[*]The combat log now displays combat data for mounted players.[/*]	[*]Repair Tables can once again be placed in Expeditions.[/*]	[*]Maxed-out specialization nodes now display the correct item power bonus.[/*][/list]
For the complete list of changes, please see the [url=https://albiononline.com/en/changelog/RISE%20OF%20AVALON%20PATCH%205][b]official patchnotes[/b][/url].

notes.title: Population Update: September 2020
notes.notes:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/1435a0abc9d9f35e1e8dddb78605e19dc1d2fbdb.jpeg[/img]

Back in May, we reported on the [url=https://albiononline.com/en/news/population-update-may-2020][b]massive population growth[/b][/url] that Albion Online saw in the first part of 2020, starting with the Queen Update in January and growing further with worldwide quarantine measures during the COVID-19 pandemic. Now, even as many of these measures are easing, the ingame population continues to grow: this month we surpassed the lockdown population peak to achieve [b]a new Daily Average User count of over 125,000 players[/b].

This boost comes in large part from the [url=https://albiononline.com/en/update/rise-of-avalon][b]Rise of Avalon Update[/b][/url], which launched on August 12 with a host of massive new features like [b]Roads of Avalon[/b], [b]Corrupted Dungeons[/b], and [b]Avalonian Weapons[/b]. The update also introduced [b]Chinese and Korean language support[/b] to the game, which has brought a huge influx of new players from these regions and grown the Albion Online community into a truly global one.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/099bf4db76d93344e515ee2d7d4f84c419e2b5bc.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Expanding the Royal Continent, Working Toward the Mobile Launch[/h3]
As mentioned in our last update, we've been focusing not only on supporting the content introduced with the Queen and Rise of Avalon updates, but also on improving the gameplay experience for all players as population numbers increase.

In tandem with new features and upgrades coming to the world of Albion over the coming months, we've set our sights on an [b]expansion of the Royal Continent[/b]. The ongoing growth of the player base has made Albion's blue, yellow and red zones fuller than ever, and we're currently hard at work on a comprehensive plan to expand these Royal zones while deepening the gameplay experience they offer.

We're also hard at work improving and streamlining the [b]mobile version[/b] of Albion Online, with continual improvements to mobile-based controls and menus being rolled out since the Queen launch, and more to come. We'll soon have further updates on the mobile version, including the next steps towards a [b]Play Store beta launch[/b] in the final leadup to the [b]official Apple and Google store launches[/b], which will finally fulfill our vision of a truly cross-platform MMORPG experience with platform-optimized content updates. For now, though, we're focusing on making the mobile experience as fun and intuitive as possible.

Thanks for being part of the ever-growing Albion Online community!

notes.title: Development Progress Update
notes.notes:
In our newest video, Albion's Game Director Robin Henkys checks in from his home office with an update on the game's development progress. After catching up with everything that's happened over the past months, he looks forward to Albion's next major content update and covers some of the major features it will contain.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Rok0ZCFRz3k
No time to watch, or prefer a written summary? Then read on...
[h3]The Queen Update[/h3]
January saw the launch of the massive and highly successful Queen update, which brought an entire new Outlands continent and numerous new high-level gameplay options to the world of Albion. Since then, we've been working nonstop to support this update, and to date we've release thirteen patches with numerous fixes and improvements:
[list]	[*]Fixing [b]critical technical issues[/b], especially for Windows 7 users[/*]	[*]Improving [b]loot and rewards[/b][/*]	[*][b]Adjusting ingame systems[/b] to make them more fun and rewarding[/*]	[*]Conducting a massive [b]Alliance test[/b] with penalties for holding more territories[/*]	[*]Updating the way [b]portals [/b]work[/*]	[*]Introducing a completely reworked [b]mobile UI [/b]and working on the stability of the mobile version[/*][/list]
We're of course continuing to support this update in various ways, including fixing exploits within the Smart Cluster Queue system and making adjustments and improvements to mount stats.
[h3]What's Next?[/h3]
Of course, everyone's here to find out what's happening with the next update. We've made a ton of progress toward the next update, far too much to cover in a single video, and soon we'll be releasing a whole series of Dev Talks with in-depth information about each topic.

Today we'll take a brief look at each of the major features that are coming. These features are in the final stages of development, and are about four weeks from being finished. With such massive features, though, we want to really take our time to make sure their implementation is as flawless as possible, so we want to make sure we test them properly. This means the next update will likely happen [b]after the end of Season 9[/b], and will be in place for the start of Season 10.

So what are some of the major features coming?
[h3]Avalonian Weapons[/h3]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/b1d5017bda55579d9c1675f4863abd06727a162c.png[/img]

One of the most anticipated features of the new update is the new [b]Avalonian Weapons[/b]. There will be [b]fifteen new weapons[/b] with entirely new spells, and even more excitingly, with [b]all-new mechanics[/b]. Examples:
[list]	[*]Avalonian Cannon: allows retargeting while the weapon is still firing[/*]	[*]Mimic: allows you to steal an enemy's ability and use it against them[/*][/list]
The new Avalonian Weapons will shake up the meta quite a bit, and unlike the current Artifact Weapons, they will be useful for all levels of play, from small-scale to large-scale combat.

These new weapons will be covered in much more detail in an upcoming Dev Talk.
[h3]Corrupted Dungeons[/h3]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/c2846ae4ef560e19147d4353690996efe56aa468.png[/img]

Another major feature coming with the next update is [b]Corrupted Dungeons[/b]. For those who missed the last Dev Talk, Corrupted Dungeons are like regular dungeons that have been [b]infected, reshaped, and taken over[/b] by demons. When a player enters, the entrance closes behind them, meaning no one can [b]directly[/b] follow them in. However, there is a way to invade these dungeons by making a pact with the demons, allowing you to hunt down players who are trying to cleanse these dungeons.

Corrupted Dungeons offer [b]an entirely new dimension of 1v1 PvP[/b] in Albion, as well as [b]an entirely new one-player PvE experience[/b] with completely new dungeon layouts, hazards, and mobs. These dungeons will also be covered at length in an upcoming Dev Talk.
[h3]Roads of Avalon[/h3]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/7f5d2e5789c5768c96e7716bf3ab3056482eacf8.png[/img]

The [b]Roads of Avalon[/b] are a massive new game feature that opens up [b]three entirely new ways of playing[/b]:
[list]	[*]They create [b]connections[/b], allowing you to find shortcuts through the world for travel, trade, and relocating.[/*]	[*]They allow [b]exploration[/b], and will contain lots of exciting new creatures to fight and resource spots to exploit.[/*]	[*]And most excitingly, players will have the opportunity to [b]live within the Roads[/b] via Hideouts, shielded somewhat from the politics of the Outlands and developing their own unique style of play.[/*][/list]
We'll have a whole mini-series of Dev Talks explaining these different features of the Roads of Avalon soon.

Thanks for joining for this special from-home talk – hopefully our upcoming videos will be from the office once again. Stay tuned for more Dev Talks coming soon!

notes.title: Queen Patch 13 is Here
notes.notes:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/c34601151414454e09d9db18cdaaa59617fe1f99.jpeg[/img]

The thirteenth patch of the Queen update is now live, bringing optimizations to the Arena system and more chances to find Solo Randomized Dungeons in blue and yellow zones. Here's what's new:
[h3]Arena Improvements[/h3]
The overall Fame earned from an Arena win has been [b]doubled[/b], from 20,000 Fame to 40,000 Fame per player on the winning team. And to make the Arena more lucrative for healers, winning players in a healing role will now receive an additional [b]Adept's Tome of Insight[/b] worth 10,000 Fame on top of the regular rewards.

Additionally, the Arena signup and notification UIs have been improved and streamlined, and clearly show the available daily rewards for each role. If you haven't played an Arena match in a while, or have yet to visit the Arena, now is the perfect time!

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/1bf4f5eeb38d5d9136326ba8d4dc94f4b2e740e1.png[/img]
[h3]More Solo Randomized Dungeons in Safe Zones[/h3]
In order to give beginner and intermediate-level players greater access to Solo Randomized Dungeons, the entrances of these dungeons in blue and yellow zones will now [b]disappear a short time after the last player enters[/b]. Once a given entry portal is removed, a new entry portal is free to spawn elsewhere in the world. This will increase the overall number of "fresh" dungeons in these zones, giving newer players greater access to the full dungeon experience while still allowing players to run solo dungeons together and follow others into a dungeon within a reasonable time window.
[h3]Zerg Changes and More[/h3]
Players waiting in a Smart Cluster Queue now [b]contribute to the total Disarray headcount[/b] in the cluster for which they are queueing, while the overall curve for the Disarray debuff now [b]accelerates more slowly[/b].

Quality-of-life improvements now include a [b]Destiny Board view prompt[/b] when a certain building type is not yet unlocked, plus improved descriptions for spells with scaled effects due to stacks.

As always, for the full details, you can check out the [url=https://albiononline.com/en/changelog/QUEEN%20PATCH%2013][b]official patchnotes[/b][/url].

notes.title: Population Update: May 2020
notes.notes:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/9e84ebc0711a79cb9eb8264690acb0d7f67610f2.jpeg[/img]

The [url=https://albiononline.com/en/update/Queen][b]Queen Update[/b][/url], released January 20, 2020, was by far the most successful Albion Online content update since launch, confirmed by consistent population growth since January and a record-high of over [b]500,000 monthly users[/b] for the month of April. Nearly six months in the making, Queen was nothing less than a complete revisioning of Albion's high-level endgame, although the new features and systems it introduced affected players of all levels and playstyles.

On a more bittersweet note, player numbers have also been affected by the lockdown and quarantine measures worldwide. We know many in the Albion Online community have been touched by the current pandemic, and are facing numerous present and future challenges. Games in general have seen a tremendous surge in popularity over the past months, and Albion Online is no exception – and as unfortunate as the reason behind it may be, we're grateful for those in our community who have stepped up to support each other, help out new players, [url=https://albiononline.com/en/news/over-40000-raised-for-charity][b]raise funds for charity[/b][/url], and make the Albion community even stronger during these uncertain times.

For us, as the developers of the game, increased player numbers mean [b]increased responsibility to all our players[/b] to ensure the game's performance remains optimal, and that gameplay remains fun, accessible, and fresh. To make sure we keep up with the increased resource demands of a growing population, we're designating [b]dedicated performance developers[/b] to make sure the game runs as smoothly as possible, and implementing [b]game design changes, balancing, and improvements[/b] with a larger player base in mind (such as the recent increase in Solo Randomized Dungeon spawns with Patch 11).

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/3f62750de37449b1711f0b1a93cc50fb439ded80.jpeg[/img]

Another positive effect of this uptrend (which started even before the Queen launch) is that it allows us to further expand our development team. Those looking to join the Sandbox Interactive team, or who know others who might be interested, can check out a list of available positions on our [url=https://albiononline.com/en/jobs][b]jobs page[/b][/url].

Thanks for your loyalty to, and support of, Albion Online over the past year. We're happy to welcome new players to the world of Albion, and very excited to bring some [url=https://albiononline.com/en/news/devtalk-whats-next][b]major new features[/b][/url] to the ever-growing world of Albion.

notes.title: The Season 9 Patch is Coming
notes.notes:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/5d596d414e91aae98bb32a524960b8383695d0a1.jpeg[/img]

On Tuesday, May 5, Queen Patch 11, also known as the [b]Season 9 Patch[/b], will go live. This patch includes numerous updates, changes, quality-of-life improvements, and bug fixes that affect nearly every aspect of gameplay. Here are some of the major changes it will bring:
[h3]A Whole New Mobile Experience[/h3]
Patch 11 brings the first version of an all new way to play Albion on mobile devices. These new mobile features apply to both iOS and Android, and include the following:
[list]	[*]A [b]virtual joystick[/b] for movement that snaps to the initial press position[/*]	[*][b]Auto-targeting[/b] of attacks and spells[/*]	[*][b]Context-based interactions[/b] with the world[/*]	[*]Updated [b]HUD layout[/b][/*]	[*]Default [b]in-game zoom level[/b] increased[/*]	[*]...and much more[/*][/list]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/94f439a9e18e7f4a2701c83d18e829b14fd72460.jpeg[/img]

For more details about these changes, including work-in-progress screenshots, please see [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/128104-Mobile-Beta-Changelog-Queen-Patch-11-Update/][b]this forum post[/b][/url].
[h3]Outlands Banks[/h3]
The shady underworld organization behind the Black Market has branched out, and now offers [b]personal bank space at numerous Outlands locations[/b]. 

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/5df965f269b954064d8d63e8a6746ea614dae14f.jpeg[/img]

Any given Outlands Bank location can be unlocked with a one-time Silver payment and used forever, and any number of locations can be unlocked. But watch out: while these banks may offer protection for your gear, they're situated in full-loot PvP zones.
[h3]Guild Season Changes[/h3]
Patch 11 brings wide-reaching changes to guild warfare in Albion. First and foremost is the new [b]Season Point and Energy Storage[/b] system, where higher-level territories hold onto a portion of all generated Season Points and Siphoned Energy until the end of the current season phase. The amount of Season Points and Energy the territory holds onto increases with its proximity to the center of the Outlands, encouraging clashes between large guilds and alliances while offering smaller guilds increased rewards for conquering and holding a territory.
[h3][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/884089b17cf05c7025ddad83a9b12051b7238230.jpeg[/img][/h3]
Other Guild Season changes include:
[list]	[*]Season Points from Veteran and World Bosses[/*]	[*]Crystal League Tokens now purchasable up to Lv.3[/*]	[*]Updated Crystal League schedule and reward pools[/*]	[*]Adjustments to Energy, Fame and Silver penalties for larger alliances[/*][/list][h3]UI and Map Improvements[/h3]
Patch 11 will introduce a wide range of quality-of-life improvements to make navigating the world of Albion much easier. UI improvements include an updated mail system, improved building interface, clearer carry capacity display, and new icons for numerous weapon skills. The world map visuals have been improved and reworked, and zones can now be viewed by prime time.

Alongside these updates, we've also been hard at work on several major upcoming features, including [b]Corrupted Dungeons [/b]and [b]Roads of Avalon[/b]. Patch 8, AKA the [b]Queen Balance Patch[/b], is here! In addition to numerous adjustments intended to improve the overall combat meta, today's patch includes some changes specifically intended to address current open-world imbalances.

Here's a partial list of some of the bigger changes:
[list]	[*][b]Mount carry weight bonuses[/b] now apply whenever the mount is equipped, not just while mounted, and carry weights now scale more accurately with the mount's item power and tier[/*]	[*][b]Disarray [/b]has been adjusted to discourage one-shot builds and army splitting[/*]	[*][b]Gathering gear[/b] skill ranges and durations have been increased to give gatherers better odds against hostile groups[/*]	[*][b]Daggers[/b] have been reworked with faster auto-attack speeds and a new Q spell; Poison Coating skill has been updated to "Bloodthirsty Blade"[/*][/list]
Combat Designer Michael Schwahn describes the intent behind these changes:

[i]"This patch contains a lot of changes to the Dagger line, a new Q ability that provides an AoE attack, and a rework of the underused one-handed Dagger. We increased the cooldown of Dash to reduce its mobility for the open world, but as many gatherers use Bloodletter and this would reduce their escape chances, we buffed the gathering gear shoe abilities to compensate. The passive buff to mount carry weights should also help gatherers and make it overall more attractive to use mounts with good carry weight.[/i]

[i]This patch also addresses the current burst-damage ZvZ items: Galatine Pair and Weeping Repeater. These items will keep their high damage potential, but it will be harder to hit as many players with them."[/i]

Here's a rundown of some of the other major changes arriving with this patch:

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/a5123f87baa91d724097dda131bf1a00a8c0458b.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Better High-Level Gathering[/h3]
After extensive player feedback, we've taken steps to improve the [b]high-level gathering experience[/b] in Albion. In addition to increasing the overall amount of T6-8 resources by 20% across the board, this patch also ups the respawn rate of these nodes, meaning once a node is located it's far more likely to be harvestable. Based on your feedback, we've also reverted the spawn behavior of small resource nodes to its state with the Queen update launch, to give a better chance of finding resources to gatherers braving high-tier zones. And on top of that, the overall small-to-large ratio has been shifted in favor of large nodes to increase the chances of finding these highly valuable gathering spots.
[h3]Open-World Optimizations[/h3]
This patch includes updates to several crucial open-world topics:
[list]	[*][b]Yellow-Zone Faction Flagging[/b]: Hostile players and faction-flagged players can no longer interact with each other in yellow zones. This is to prevent the case where hostile players would knock down faction-flagged players, who were then executed by enemy factions, resulting in a lucrative ganking opportunity with zero risk.[/*]	[*][b]Invisibility Shrines[/b]:Click priority for Invisibility Shrines in Outlands Portal Zones is now prioritized over player corpses and loot, to prevent a case where players could not use the shrines while still allowing optional looting after use.[/*]	[*][b]Hellgate Settings[/b]: Hellgates now spawn every 6-10 minutes, offering more reliable opportunities to participate. Fame has also been shifted from the sub-boss demons to the final boss, and its loot (and that of the final chest) are now protected for the party dealing the most damage to reward those who do the heavy PvE lifting.[/*][/list]
As always, you can read the full list of changes and fixes in the [url=https://albiononline.com/en/changelog/QUEEN%20PATCH%208][b]official patchnotes[/b][/url].

notes.title: Patch 7 is Here
notes.notes:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/6e83d4590d02964b61e4959a2d58412b24d73848.jpeg[/img]

Today's patch brings further changes and improvements to several essential issues. First and foremost is the second part of our previously announced alliance limit test, reduced [b]Silver and Fame[/b] for members of alliances with 10+ territories. We've also further improved the [b]loot experience in all randomized dungeons[/b], and added [b]invisibility shrines and additional exits[/b] to Outlands portal zones to give players a bit of protection when entering Albion's black zones.

[h3]Alliance Limitations Update[/h3]
Since the launch of the Queen update in January, we've put a great deal of effort into countering the outsized effect of mega-alliances in Albion. Patch 5 introduced a [b]Siphoned Energy Drain[/b] on guilds and alliances with [b]10 or more territories[/b] that was intended to force large alliances to consider the costs when claiming large numbers of territories. With today's patch, all players in these guilds and alliances will receive [b]reduced Silver and Fame income[/b].

Both these new systems are part of our current [b]alliance limit test[/b] - for more information, please see [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/124568][b]this forum post[/b][/url].

[h3]Better Dungeon Loot[/h3]
Based on community feedback, we've decided to increase the appearance of higher-tier loot in high-level dungeons to make sure these challenging settings have equally worthwhile rewards. More specifically, T7 dungeons will only have [b]T5 loot and higher[/b] and T8 dungeons will only have [b]T6 loot and higher[/b]. This was accomplished by shifting the Black Market's allocated Silver to higher-tier items, while keeping the overall Silver value of chests the same.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/f617c25545a421977d5ee39c3bfa01a9b52481a4.jpeg[/img]

[h3]Anti-Ganking Measures in Portal Zones[/h3]
Based on community feedback that [b]gankers in Outlands Portal Zones[/b] (the very first zones entered when passing through a Realmgate) made these areas far more dangerous than their higher-level counterparts, we've implemented various changes with this patch. It was never intended that any player's first moments in the Outlands should be the most challenging, and as such these features will give new Outlands arrivals a fighting chance.

Here's what's been added:
[list]	[*][b]Invisibility Shrines[/b] have been added to the immediate area around each Outlands portal[/*]	[*]These shrines have also been placed by each [b]exit [/b]from the portal zone[/*]	[*]Each portal zone has a total of [b]four exits[/b] to avoid bottlenecks[/*][/list]
For full details of these changes and the intentions behind them, please see [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/125487][b]this forum post[/b][/url].

As always, you can read the full list of changes and fixes in the [url=https://albiononline.com/en/changelog/QUEEN%20PATCH%207][b]official patchnotes[/b][/url].

notes.title: Patch 6 Brings Loot Updates
notes.notes:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/f5a3b06437338f771ec5235e1fba54e941fd7492.jpeg[/img]

Today's patch - part of an ambitious weekly update schedule that started with the launch of the Queen update - brings improvements to the Elite Dungeon experience, lower fast-travel costs, and more.

[h3]Elite Dungeon Changes[/h3]
In the first of several changes intended to improve the loot experience in Randomized Dungeons, the drop rate of [b]Avalonian Artifacts in Elite Dungeons[/b] is now approximately [b]double[/b] what it was before. And to reduce the time needed to complete these dungeons, the health and damage of all Avalonian enemies has been slightly reduced across the board.
[h3]Knockdown Loot Loss Changes[/h3]
Items without a durability stat, such as resources, will no longer have a chance to be [b]destroyed upon knockdown[/b]. This change is intended to help avoid situations where players were confused about what happened to items in their inventory. It should also improve the [b]overall loot experience in Elite Dungeons[/b], where a large percent of loot was previously destroyed by being knocked down repeatedly.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/7136d52585b8a93f48ee8bdf920a76e578cb0e9d.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Travel Cost Modifier Changes[/h3]
With this patch, travel cost modifiers for resources, laborer journals, and luxury goods have been updated, leading to reduced [b]travel and Hideout retrieval costs[/b] for nearly all tiers of these items. This is only a [b]first step[/b] in reviewing fast travel cost modifiers - we will continue to review these costs, and may adjust them further in future patches.
[h3]Other Changes and Fixes[/h3][list]	[*]Cooldown on [b]rejoining an alliance[/b] raised from 3 days to 7 days[/*]	[*]Introduced time penalty on [b]repeated respawns in Hideouts[/b] to prevent overuse of repeated-suicide defense strategies[/*]	[*]Players can now join the Smart Cluster Queue while mounted[/*][/list]
As always, you can read the complete list of changes in the [url=https://albiononline.com/en/changelog/QUEEN%20PATCH%206][b]official patchnotes[/b][/url].

notes.title: Patch 5 is Alive!
notes.notes:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/61c7d63f1ecc5a41967303bc6a7048548ba7fe13.jpeg[/img]

As announced in a [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/124568][b]recent forum post[/b][/url], we are looking at ways to limit the influence of large alliances in Albion. With today's patch (the fifth weekly patch since the launch of the Queen update!), we have implemented the first part of this test: [b]Siphoned Energy Drain[/b].

[h3]Siphoned Energy Drain[/h3]
This debuff gives reduced Siphoned Energy gains to all alliances and unallied single guilds that have ten or more territories, with each additional territory beyond ten further decreasing energy earned by 5%. Along with adjustments to the Smart Cluster Queue and Zerg Debuff (see below), this change is intended to make larger alliances and guilds consider carefully whether holding higher quantities of territories is worthwhile.

The second part of this test, [b]Fame and Silver Penalties[/b] for members of alliances and guilds with over 10 territories, will come with [b]Queen Patch 6[/b]. This patch has an expected launch date of [b]Wednesday, March 4[/b].

You can read further details on the [url=https://albiononline.com/en/changelog/QUEEN%20PATCH%205][b]official patchnotes page[/b][/url].

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/acc39108365cce7f52da3137554553dbfba8d029.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Other Changes and Fixes[/h3]
Patch 5 brings additional changes intended to limit the influence of large armies, as well as fixes and polishing:
[list]	[*]Minimum average IP for Smart Cluster Queue reduced from 800 to 700[/*]	[*]Zerg Debuff ("Disarray") values increase more quickly for larger armies[/*]	[*]Cooldown implemented on rejoining dropped guilds and alliances[/*]	[*]Transmutation times significantly reduced[/*]	[*]Ability to fast travel to "Home" locations[/*]	[*]Ability to retrieve items from Hideouts that can no longer be accessed[/*]	[*]Small Tier 7 and Tier 8 nodes now spawn fully charged[/*]	[*]Removed unnecessary warnings when picking up farmed items[/*][/list]
We'll be deploying additional patches in the coming weeks to bring even more improvements and fixes to the game. As always, we welcome your feedback on [url=https://discordapp.com/invite/albiononline][b]Discord[/b][/url] or our [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/][b]forums[/b][/url]!

notes.title: Patch 3 is Here
notes.notes:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/919c9fea08dc3bcf7449293dbc90aff5245bc4f7.jpeg[/img]

The third weekly patch since the launch of the Queen update is now live, bringing a much-requested update to Outlands respawn behavior along with various bug fixes. Most importantly, Outland towns are [b]no longer classified as visited cities[/b] when choosing "Last City" as a respawn option. This allows players to respawn from Outlands to a Royal city, whereas previously players could find themselves "stuck" in an Outland town, as the only way to get out was by walking to a portal several zones away.

Players based in the Outlands can now also [b]travel more freely to the Royals[/b]. Here's how it works:
[list]	[*]Players who base themselves in one of the Outland towns or a Hideout can now essentially "fast-travel" back to the Royals to visit their islands, do farming, etc.[/*]	[*]This is done by dying in the Outlands (either in a fight or via /suicide) and respawning in "Last City" in the Royals, [b]which no longer removes the "Home" respawn setting[/b][/*]	[*]The "Home" respawn setting is removed when a player chooses to re-enter the Outlands via a Realmgate[/*][/list]
Thus, while this new system gives players options to base themselves in the Outlands and continue using the Royals at the same time, it [b]does not[/b] allow them to move forces back and forth between two Outlands access points. To illustrate this, under this new system you [b]could not[/b] do the following:
[list]	[*]Be in a Hideout[/*]	[*]Die and respawn in a Royal city[/*]	[*]Go through the city's Realmgate[/*]	[*]Attack a territory near the Outland portal[/*]	[*]Die and respawn back at your Hideout to execute another attack[/*][/list]
These changes are intended to give Outlands players easier and more streamlined access to the Royals, [b]without giving them unfair advantages[/b] in power projection, logistics, and transport.

For more background on these changes, as well as an idea of our future plans for streamlining and updating this system, please see [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/123555][b]this forum post[/b][/url].

For precise details of this change, as well as a complete list of bug fixes, please see the [url=https://albiononline.com/en/changelog/QUEEN%20PATCH%203][b]official patch notes[/b][/url].

notes.title: The Queen Update Arrives January 20
notes.notes:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/2ddb70c883888e95cf504851edf80e0177cfcec3.jpeg[/img]

[b]Queen[/b] is coming! This update brings a [b]complete rework of the Outlands continent[/b] along with fully revamped [b]open-world territory control[/b]. [b]Hideouts[/b] let guilds place their own bases in the open world, and the new [b]Crystal League[/b] allows players of all levels to participate in 5v5 battles. This update also introduces a new elite faction to the game: the [b]Avalonians[/b]. Found in the new [b]Elite Randomized Dungeons[/b], the Avalonians offer incredible rewards to those who can best them, including week-long PvE Fame buffs and new [b]Artifact Armors[/b]. And on top of all this, Queen also brings a huge number of [b]quality-of-life improvements[/b] to streamline and strengthen numerous aspects of the game.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/7df637df4e6730b79d669c9124eaa30ce732edbf.jpeg[/img]
[h3]A New Era for Albion's Guilds[/h3]
Queen brings a complete rework of the [b]Outlands[/b], allowing guilds of different strengths to compete at their own levels and fulfilling the next major milestone in Albion Online's journey to become the ultimate sandbox MMO. [b]Hideouts [/b]allow guilds to build their own underground bases in the open world, and [b]open-world battles[/b] bring new opportunities for large-scale combat.

Together, these massive new systems allow every guild member to contribute to their guild's strength and progress. And the new [b]Crystal League[/b] system allows players of all levels to engage in 5v5 combat, with elite players able to unlock tremendous rewards for their guilds.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/7a1ba3b25e4d188982fc836194623557205e9b93.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Avalonians and Elite Dungeons
[/h3]Queen brings a completely new faction, the ancient and powerful [b]Avalonians[/b], to the world of Albion. These elite enemies can be challenged in [b]Elite Randomized Dungeons[/b] that appear throughout the Outlands, providing a high-level challenge to groups of 15-20 players, and offering incredible rewards like [b]week-long PvE Fame buffs[/b] and shards that can be crafted into the most powerful [b]Artifact Armor[/b] in the game.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/b80f12963d9586f339a16d855819fa4cb2a23b95.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Numerous Quality-of-Life Improvements
[/h3]Along with a huge new [b]Wardrobe Skin[/b] system, Queen brings numerous additional features and improvements to the game, such as:
[list]	[*][b]Enchanted stone[/b] with improved refining efficiency[/*]	[*][b]New cursors[/b] for improved visibility[/*]	[*][b]Keyboard shortcut[/b] to inspect players[/*]	[*][b]Simplified and streamlined[/b] Item Power progression[/*]	[*]Updated [b]World Boss icons[/b][/*]	[*]...and much, much more[/*][/list]
For a complete rundown of everything coming with this massive content update, please visit the [url=https://albiononline.com/en/update/Queen][b]official update page[/b][/url].

notes.title: Player and Item Migration with the Queen Update
notes.notes:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/16b7aec4c97ea3ec5a7841121d77c2109d4b6d35.jpeg[/img]

The Queen update arrives on [b]January 20, 2020[/b]. With this update, the [b]Outlands [/b]will be completely reworked, and with very few exceptions, [b]all territories and siege camps in the Royal Continent will be removed[/b]. We have put a number of measures in place to assist with this transition, but as there is the potential for item loss, please read the following changes carefully.
[h1]Migrating Players and Items[/h1]
[b]1. Players:[/b]
[list]	[*]Players in the [b]Outlands [/b]will be moved to the city with the portal closest to them. Even though the Caerleon portals will no longer exist, for this transfer, Caerleon is included among these cities.[/*]	[*]Players in [b]affected zones in the Royal continent[/b] (i.e. those that had [b]territories or siege camps[/b]) will be moved to the nearest zone entrance.[/*][/list]
[b]2. Banks and Battlevaults:[/b]
[list]	[*]All personal items in [b]banks and battlevaults[/b] in the Outlands, or in a removed Royal Territory or Siege Camp, will be [b]moved to the Royal City that is closest or has the closest portal[/b].[/*]	[*][b]Guild banks in territories[/b] will be moved to the owning guild's [b]Guild Island Bank[/b].[/*]	[*]Territory bank [b]tabs [/b](and their corresponding access rights) will be copied to the Guild Island Bank.[/*]	[*]If the guild doesn't own a Guild Island, [b]the items will be destroyed[/b].[/*][/list]
[b]3. Islands:[/b]
[list]	[*]Personal and guild islands [b]will be movable[/b] during the month following the Queen update. This is currently slated for January 20 10:01 UTC to February 20 10:00 UTC.[/*]	[*]Only islands created prior to the launch of the Queen update are eligible to be moved.[/*]	[*]Islands moved during the last island move are still eligible to be moved once more after the Queen update.[/*][/list]
[b]4. Items that will NOT be moved:[/b]
[list]	[*]Items currently for sale or in the completed tab of [b]Marketplaces in Guild Home Territories [/b]will [b]not[/b] be moved. This means that any items in Marketplaces in the Outlands when Queen goes live [b]will be lost[/b].[/*]	[*]Contents of placeable chests, as well as all placed furniture items, [b]will not be moved[/b] and will be destroyed.[/*]	[*][b]Farmable items left in territories[/b] will be destroyed.[/*]	[*][b]Buildings left in territories[/b], including farms and pastures, will be destroyed.[/*][/list]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/4f393a4cbb15580ed778f197571cc44677461722.jpeg[/img]
[h1]Amnesty for Low Reputations[/h1]
With the changes to the Outlands, and particularly the destruction of the Caerleon Realmgate, movement restrictions due to reputation will be mitigated as follows:
[list]	[*]Players below -15000 reputation [b]will have their reputation adjusted to -15000[/b] to allow movement within [b]yellow and red zones[/b].[/*]	[*]However, as Caerleon will no longer have a Realmgate to the Outlands, if a Dreaded player enters Caerleon (after re-lowering their reputation in a neighboring red zone), their [b]only options[/b] are to wait for their reputation to increase or fast travel to another city.[/*][/list]

notes.title: Percival Patch 11 is Here
notes.notes:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/7f14f2a3213092000075494289c2f833e336e6dd.jpeg[/img]

The [url=https://albiononline.com/en/news/outlands-report-1-threats-and-opportunities][b]Avalonian Invasion[/b][/url] is in full swing, guilds are battling it out in a unique standalone season... and [b]Percival Patch 11[/b] is here! Today's patch brings several important updates to combat in Albion, in particular:
[list]	[*]The [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/119764-Disarray-Zerg-Debuff/?postID=964642#post964642][b]zerg debuff[/b][/url] values have been updated to more effectively reward smaller armies[/*]	[*]Zerg debuffs no longer apply [b]during GvGs[/b], regardless of how many allied players are in the territory[/*]	[*][b]Healing Sickness[/b] duration has been increased [/*]	[*][b]Siege Ballista[/b] damage has been increased[/*]	[*]Numerous other melee, ranged, and magic skills have been updated [/*][/list]
Michael Schwahn, Combat Designer for Albion Online, describes the intent behind these changes: "We wanted to shake up the healer meta a bit, and to push the siege ballista as a viable counter to other battle mounts. We also felt it was time to reduce the utility of Parry Strike, in order to open up more of a variety with bruiser builds." These changes will play out over the remainder of the standalone season, which [b][url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/119885-Standalone-Event-Season-Schedule/]runs until January 20[/url][/b].

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/25013791e08866c048f55e7fc25bd17ac2e12be3.jpeg[/img]
[h1]Additional Changes[/h1]
In a first for the world of Albion, [b]Uncle Frost[/b] now appears as a boss in certain rare dungeons! Group and solo [b]Keeper Randomized Dungeons[/b] in all zones have a chance to end in a special [b]Yuletide Dungeon[/b], where you'll face off against this mysterious foe. Beat him to unlock Christmas-themed loot, including a chance at holiday-themed [b]mount skins[/b].

Also with today's patch, a new [b]Adventurer Avatar[/b] is available at the Vanity Merchant. This new item joins the [b]Adventurer Avatar Ring[/b] in a growing list of vanity items – trade in unclaimed Adventurer's Challenge Avatar Rings for Adventurer Tokens to unlock these new items!

For a complete list of changes, please see the [url=https://albiononline.com/en/changelog/PERCIVAL%20PATCH%2011][b]official changelog[/b][/url].

notes.title: Percival Patch 7 is Here
notes.notes:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/6kp5Ici.png[/img]

Today we launched [b]Percival Patch 7[/b], which brings changes to Albion's Silver sinks, quality-of-life improvements to building and transmuting, updated resource spawn rates, and more. So what's new?
[h1]More Silver Sinks[/h1]
With today's patch, we've increased the [b]Silver costs assessed by the system[/b] for various activities. These system-based costs serve as Silver sinks, which keep the overall quantity of Silver in the world of Albion consistent, and prevent runaway inflation of the Silver-to-Gold ratio. With the introduction of [b]Randomized Dungeons[/b] in the Oberon update, the amount of Silver in the game increased tremendously, leading to inflated Gold costs for those looking to trade in their Silver. These updated costs mean the amount of Silver leaving the economy is once again in line with the amount entering it.

This patch brings the following cost changes:
[list]	[*]Increased repair costs of all items by 100%, but halved knockdown damage (from 10% to 5%), meaning repair cost of knockdowns remains the same[/*]	[*]Increased Market Order Fee from 1% to 1.5%[/*]	[*]Increased Market Tax from 4% to 6% (from 2% to 3% with Premium)[/*]	[*]Increased the cost of buying additional bank tabs by 50%[/*]	[*]Increased the cost of buying and upgrading islands by 50%[/*]	[*]Increased the cost of converting Fame to Fame Credits by 50%[/*]	[*]Increased the cost of using the fast travel feature by 50%[/*]	[*]Reduced the rate at which Silver offers are generated by the Black Market by 10%[/*][/list][h1]Transmutation Changes[/h1]
In addition to the changes listed above, we've rebalanced the cost structure for [b]transmutation.[/b] Transmutation was always intended as a natural ingame sink, but was previously so expensive that it was almost never used. This patch [b]lowers[/b] overall costs for transmutation, while also making the transmutation process [b]four times faster[/b], in order to make it more appealing. With decreased Silver (and time!) costs for transmutation, this previously overlooked activity should become a more viable option.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/P1E0msv.png[/img]
[h1]Builders Rejoice![/h1]
Along with the increased speed of transmutation, constructing, upgrading, and repairing buildings is now [b]twice as fast[/b]. Construction and maintenance already require a great deal of resources, so we've decided to make the actual processes of building creation and upkeep less time-consuming for players who have already made the necessary resource commitment.
[h1]Keeping Albion Balanced[/h1]
Last but not least, we've also made some changes to keep the game's [b]gathering and combat[/b] balanced. Resources and "resource critters" in tier 2, 3, and 4 blue zones now take[b] twice as long[/b] to respawn, to avoid flooding the market with low-tier resources. On the combat side, we've made various changes, including [b]reducing the impact of Damnation bomb squads[/b] in ZvZs and removing the option to stack Quarrier Boots via Self-Ignition, which gave gankers an undue advantage.

You can read the detailed list of changes in the [url=https://albiononline.com/en/changelog/PERCIVAL%20PATCH%207][b]official patchnotes[/b][/url].

notes.title: Dev Talk: Queen Update Introduction
notes.notes:
In our most recent Dev Talk, Robin Henkys, Game Director of Albion Online, offers a first look at some of the huge changes coming to the Outlands with the next major content update, [b]Queen[/b]. Much of the Outlands rework is still in the early stages of development, but we want to introduce various parts of it now to give a "big-picture" view of this long-anticipated change. While the next update will have numerous additional features, the Outlands rework is central to our vision of bringing a true hardcore sandbox experience to our players.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=C5bmUuyQo_o

No time to watch the video, or prefer a written summary? Read on for all the details of his talk.
[h1]Filling in the Roadmap[/h1]
In our last Dev Talk, we set out how we're still proceeding with the roadmap we laid out earlier this year. This is still true, and in addition we have more exciting new content planned which we’ll talk about in the future.

Today, though, we want to get more specifically into our plans for the [b]Outlands [/b]and what we’re working on for the next content update, code-named [b]Queen[/b]. The Outlands rework is a major milestone of the Roadmap, and it consists of [b]five major improvements[/b] we’re planning to introduce in the next update:
[list]	[*]An [b]entirely new Outlands map[/b][/*]	[*]The ability to freely build [b]Guild Hideouts[/b] in the Outlands to live deep in the wilds of Albion[/*]	[*]A [b]new method for territory control[/b] which allows all guild members to help capture a territory instead of being limited to five players[/*]	[*][b]Improved 5v5 Crystal Realm battles[/b] with the ability to participate even if you don’t own a territory, but with additional bonuses for those who do[/*]	[*][b]Zerg debuffs[/b] and the [b]smart cluster queue[/b][/*][/list]
All these changes listed together makes for some big changes coming to Albion Online, so let's take a closer look at each of them and explain what they are, what function they serve in the game, why we’re excited about them.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/GVy3ITY.png[/img]
[h1]1. The New Outlands Map[/h1]
When we first designed our current [b]Outlands map[/b], our main concern was adding as much distance between the low and high Outlands as possible. This created a "stretched" map, with the highest-value areas at one end and the weakest areas at the other.

In reality, though, we saw guilds settling wherever there was available space. The overarching problem was that guilds had no reasonable means of progression to the top area, [b]Mercia[/b].

Here's how the new Outlands map will be different:
[list]	[*]In the new Outlands, [b]the most valuable areas in the game will be at the center of the map[/b], leaving it open to attack and raids from all sides[/*]	[*]Not only the center of the map will be highly attractive: high value areas will also be [b]mixed into the entire world[/b] to create local hotspots of fighting and conflict[/*]	[*]The number of territories in each zone will be reduced from two to one (see section 3 below for more info)[/*][/list]
Also, with the launch of this new world,[b] the Caerleon portal will collapse[/b] and the Outlands will no longer be accessible from Caerleon. As with the last portal change, players will be given another opportunity to move their islands should they want to. We plan on revisiting the role of Caerleon in a future update.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/Gv9DKwd.jpg[/img]
[h1]2. Hideouts[/h1]
You may have heard us talking about Hideouts before. We’re very excited about them, and today we'll give you an introductory overview to this major new feature.

[b]What are Hideouts, and how are they placed?[/b]
[list]	[*]Hideouts are [b]buildable bases[/b] guilds can place [b]anywhere in the Outlands[/b][/*]	[*]They start out as a [b]Hideout Building Kit[/b], a craftable item that is quite heavy and needs to be transported to the location you want to place the Hideout[/*]	[*]Once placed, the Hideout construction site [b]has to be defended[/b] for a short time before becoming invulnerable for about a day[/*]	[*]The next day, just before construction finishes, the Hideout [b]becomes vulnerable for another short period[/b] before it finally becomes established[/*]	[*]These attack phases prevent guilds from aggressively “sneaking” Hideouts into their enemies’ backyards[/*][/list]
[b]Once a Hideout is established, how does it work?[/b]
[list]	[*]Once the Hideout is established, it can be entered by [b]anyone the owning guild grants permission to[/b][/*]	[*]Inside, you can [b]build crafting stations, store your equipment, set a respawn point and have a Marketplace[/b][/*]	[*]Hideouts can be [b]upgraded[/b][/*][/list]
Basically the Hideouts allow any guild to have a fully functional base anywhere in the Outlands. You could even grant visiting rights to all players and build [b]your own Outlands city[/b] with public crafting stations, Marketplaces, and so on. We're very excited about the tremendous sandbox potential of this system, and we look forward to seeing what players do with it.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/orZftm5.jpg[/img]
[h1]3. Open-World Territory Battles[/h1]
The next change is likely the most controversial, but it is one that we have been thinking about for a very long time. Along with the introduction of Hideouts, we are removing the 5v5 GvG battle system from territory control, and replacing it with a battle system that allows all members of a guild to contribute to help claim territories.
[list]	[*]Under the new system, attacking a territory requires you to [b]declare a challenge in the open world[/b]. At any point during the day, you can ride to your enemies’ territory, kill their guards and challenge control of the territory.[/*]	[*]This will [b]schedule a battle[/b] during the prime time on the following day. During the next day’s battle, the defenders can try to remove the attacker’s claim by channeling the territory tower.[/*]	[*]The attackers, on the other hand, can claim the territory by channeling the tower themselves.[/*]	[*]Note that it is entirely possible for [b]multiple groups to challenge control of the same territory at the same time[/b], enabling three-plus way battles for territory control.[/*]	[*]Finally, since armies can attack multiple territories at the same time, bringing all your forces to bear on the same territory may not be the smartest move.[/*][/list]
This change finally enables all players of a guild to support their guild’s bid for territory control. It also removes territory control from those players simply seeking the thrill of 5v5 battles, who may not actually care about territories and simply want thrill of the battle itself.

For these players, and everyone who loves high-risk 5v5 action in Albion, we have a special treat: an [b]expanded Crystal Realm Battle system[/b] with many opportunities for high-end PvP action.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/q49Ht3Z.png[/img]
[h1]4. Expanded Crystal Realm Battles[/h1]
Under the new, expanded Crystal Realm Battle system, players can participate in [b]high-stakes 5v5 fights, regardless of whether their guild holds a territory[/b].

Instead, players earn their participation by acquiring a [b]Crystal Realm Token[/b]. These tokens exist in multiple levels, and at different times during the day, the week, and the month, battles of different levels matching these tokens will take place. Players who wish to participate in these battles will need to collect a group of five players, each of whom has a token of the same level.

If they win, they earn a [b]significant reward[/b] and the token they were using is [b]upgraded to the next level[/b]. If they lose, their token is [b]destroyed[/b].

The exciting thing about this system is that it allows [b]players without strong guilds[/b] to still participate in exciting, high-risk 5v5 fights, while still ensuring [b]guilds with strong 5v5 players[/b] will continue to reap benefits.

Players can sign up for a Crystal Realm Battle in two different ways:
[list]	[*]They can go to the [b]Energy Manipulator NPC[/b] in any city or upgraded Hideout, or[/*]	[*]They can go enter the Crystal Realm via the tower of an[b] owned territory[/b].[/*][/list]
Whichever way they choose, they are thrown into a Crystal Realm Battle and face off against another team. However, if they sign up via a territory tower and win, they will [b]upgrade the power of the territory crystal[/b], which has the following effects:
[list]	[*]It adds a [b]general gathering buff [/b]for all guild members gathering within the affected territory[/*]	[*]The [b]percentage of enchanted resources[/b] around the territory is increased[/*]	[*]It [b]buffs the territory guards[/b], making it harder for enemies to attack the territory in the open world[/*][/list]
This territory upgrade effect means that you can still benefit significantly from having a strong 5v5 team in your guild.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/niFKHC6.png[/img]
[h1]5. Zerg Debuffs and the Smart Cluster Queue[/h1]
With so many features coming that involve open-world battles, you’re probably wondering how we’re going to deal with all the players these massive battles will involve.

[b]1. Smart Cluster Queue System[/b]

The Smart Cluster Queue system prevents large armies from blocking entire zones by overcrowding them. Essentially, this system analyzes how many players from one side are attempting to enter a zone, and calculates based on the players' gear and status how much they're contributing to the fight. It then checks how many players the other side has and how many want to enter the same area, and auto-balances the zone based on the number of players on each side. Excess players are moved to nearby zones, where they can continue the fight in secondary battles.

[b]2. Zerg Debuff[/b]

This system adds an "inefficiency" tradeoff to bringing too many people to a fight. Whenever more than 25 allied players are in the same zone, these players will suffer from an “inefficiency” debuff that decreases their combat effectiveness slightly. The more players in your army, the more this debuff increases. This means you will have to choose an optimal army size based on your guilds’ size and abilities, and should not simply collect the largest army in one place.

***

We’ll continue providing more details on each of these features as development continues, hopefully with a dedicated video for each feature. With this talk, you should at least have a good overview of what changes are coming with the Queen update, and how they will work together to completely redefine the experience of living in the Outlands and fighting for territories.

For now, we hope you're excited for these new opportunities for epic large-scale and 5v5 fights, and the ability for guilds of all sizes to live in the Outlands. That's all for today - thanks for watching, and stay tuned for more Dev Talks over the coming weeks!

notes.title: The Percival Midseason Patch is Here
notes.notes:
Today we launched Percival Patch 5, also known as the Percival Midseason Patch. Here's a rundown of some of the changes and improvements it brings:

[img]https://i.imgur.com/Ykv6B1K.png[/img]
[h1]Meta Changes and Updated Spells[/h1]
The patch brings changes across a wide range of weapon and armor spells, with some specific goals in mind. "One of our primary goals with this patch was to reduce the impact of dive comps," says Michael Schwahn, Combat Designer for Albion Online. "And while we buffed a few underused items, this patch brings quite a few nerfs. The recent trend toward buffing items was shifting the gameplay away from our intended direction, so these changes are intended to ground the gameplay a bit."

The patch also brings several new and updated spells. The new Fire Staff spell,[b] Fire Artillery[/b], launches a cannon-like stationary attack on a target that inflicts ongoing burn damage and stacked debuffs. The Nature Staff spell Poison Thorns has been reworked: now simply called [b]Thorns[/b], it has moved from the W to the Q slot and gives 5 stacks that deal additional magic damage to targets.

Finally, [b]Healing Sickness[/b] is a new debuff intended to prevent solo healers from sustaining their own HP indefinitely. As healing another target immediately cancels the debuff, this change should only affect solo and small-scale PvP.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/sigAEfk.png[/img]
[h1]New Guild Logs[/h1]
Today's patch also introduces new and improved guild logs for several long-requested categories:
[list]	[*]Players [b]joining and leaving[/b] the guild,[/*]	[*]Players being [b]invited to or kicked from[/b] the guild, and[/*]	[*][b]Guild role[/b] changes, including who made the change.[/*][/list]
These logs are accompanied by an updated UI, which, in addition to being more attractive and easier to read, also allows for longer lists of names. For more information about the updated guild logs and our plans for future improvements, please see this [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/118236][b]forum post[/b][/url].

[img]https://i.imgur.com/sSWQkoF.png[/img]
[h1]Updated Mobs[/h1]
Randomized Dungeon mob spells have been balanced and reworked, with many of them receiving improved animations and spell effects for clearer feedback during combat. Affected mobs include the [b]Heretic Brawler[/b], the [b]Undead Governor[/b], and several [b]Keeper bosses[/b], along with the [b]Keeper Bear[/b] and [b]Keeper Stump[/b].

[b]Additional Patch 5 Changes:[/b]
[list]	[*]Updated parameters for crafting station fees[/*]	[*]Updated names of mount skin unlocks to include base mounts + improved Trash item description[/*]	[*]New icon for Cleanse spell[/*]	[*]Numerous fixes related to combat, respawning, terrain, animation, audio, and localization[/*][/list]
For a complete list of the changes launching with today's patch, please see the [url=https://albiononline.com/en/changelog/PERCIVAL%20PATCH%205][b]official patchnotes[/b][/url].

notes.title: Changelong: Percival Update
notes.notes:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/6680a76.jpg[/img]
[h1]Percival Update - Ver. 1.15.382 / REV 145855 - 10 July 2019[/h1]

[h1]Features[/h1]
[b]Solo Randomized Dungeons[/b]

Randomized Dungeons balanced for solo players will now appear throughout the open world, and will be distinguishable from group randomized dungeons by their portal-like appearance. Higher-tier solo dungeons can be accessed via special Dungeon Maps, which can be obtained from mob drops or bought from other players through the Marketplace.

[b]New Character Customization Options [/b]

Players now have a larger number of customization options for their characters, including numerous hair, beard, face, and underwear options. Character appearance can now be updated at any time, from anywhere in the world.

For more details on character customization, please see this forum post: [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/112754]https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/112754[/url]

[b]Mount Skins[/b]

Mounts skins can now be used to alter the appearance of a player's active mount. Once unlocked, a mount skin is bound to the account and can be used by all characters. With Percival, numerous rare mounts will be converted to skins, and additional new skins will be unlockable with Gold.

For more details, including a list of pre-Percival mounts that will be converted to skins, please see this forum post: [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/112754]https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/112754[/url]

[b]New Mobs and Shrines[/b]

New mob types have been added to solo and group Randomized Dungeons for all factions. These include new trap- and nest-type opponents, as well as environmental hazards like explosives. Solo Randomized Dungeons introduce small combat shrines, which give a random combat buff to the first player who activates them, offering advantages in both PvE and PvP.

[b]New Weapon Skills[/b]

Seven new skills have been added to a range of player weapons:
[list]	[*]Axes: Spinning Blades[/*]	[*]Frost Staffs: Ice Shard[/*]	[*]Hammers: Inertia Ring[/*]	[*]Nature Staffs: Rejuvenating Breeze[/*]	[*]Quarterstaffs: Rising Blow[/*]	[*]Spears: Impaler[/*]	[*]Swords: Parry[/*][/list]
For details of these skills, see the Combat Balance Changes section below.

[b]Upgradeable Bank Tabs[/b]

Additional tabs can now be added to both personal banks (i.e. those found in cities) AND guild / territory vaults, with the following specifications:
[list]	[*]City Banks: up to 14 additional personal tabs can be purchased for Silver[/*]	[*]Guild Banks: up to 14 additional personal tabs AND 14 additional guild tabs can be purchased for Silver[/*]	[*]Territory Banks: new private tabs are not available, but 5 guild tabs can be purchased for a total of 14 tabs[/*]	[*]Homeplot Banks are now structured like Guild Island Banks (same total weight and slots)[/*]	[*]Siege Camps and Guild City Banks do not receive any additional tabs[/*]	[*]The first personal bank tab is always the first to open in banks and guild vaults[/*][/list][h1]Improvements[/h1]
[b]Audio Improvements[/b]
[list]	[*]Polished and updated spell effect sounds for Quarterstaffs, Axes, Spears, Daggers, Hammers and Maces based on spell intensity[/*]	[*]Master Volume fader added to Audio Settings UI[/*]	[*]Added new voiceovers to Artifact Foundry NPC[/*][/list]
[b]Other Improvements[/b]
[list]	[*]Character appearance has been greatly improved for unclothed male and female character models[/*]	[*]New language channels have been created for every supported language - players will join the channel that matches their client language[/*]	[*]Date formats can now be set via the "Language" UI[/*]	[*]Up to five emotes can now be assigned to Hotkeys in the Settings menu[/*]	[*]Reworked character location markers and random dungeon markers on worldmap[/*]	[*]Players can now choose whether to automatically transfer newly-purchased items directly from the Marketplace to their inventory (in cases where inventory is full, items will be sent to the "Completed" tab as normal)[/*]	[*]New terrain and level templates created for Solo Randomized Dungeons have been added to Group Randomized Dungeons as well[/*]	[*]Seven new achievements based on Randomized Dungeons and Customization have been added[/*][/list][h1]Changes[/h1]
[b]Crystal and City GvG Changes[/b]

Crystal Realm GvGs are now available between seasons. These between-season fights do not generate season points, but still offer loot and rewards.

The threshold for which money invested in 20v20 city GvGs is returned has been adjusted from [b]149 points to 195 points[/b]. Since points are scored on a subtractive basis, this means that attackers now need to [b]score fewer points[/b] to get their Silver back. Additionally, match length for city GvGs has been [b]increased from 25 minutes to 30 minutes[/b].

City GvGs have been added to the practice GvG "scrims" available. To initiate a practice city fight, one party of 20 must invite another party of 20 using the regular chat commands (see [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/86776][b]here[/b][/url] for more info). The new map name is "city".

[b]Mob Changes[/b]

Higher-tier mobs now have [b]more armor instead of more health[/b] to compensate for the player's Reaver bonus damage. This means player damage dealt to mobs will be more or less equal across tiers - for example, if you deal 100 damage versus a tier 4 mob you will deal 90 damage versus a tier 8 mob. Previously, if you dealt 100 damage versus Tier 4 you would deal 400 damage versus Tier 8.

notes.title: The Percival Update Arrives July 10!
notes.notes:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/4uJiFXZ.jpg[/img]

[b]Percival [/b]is coming! The seventh major post-release content update for Albion Online brings long-requested [b]Solo Randomized Dungeons[/b], a variety of major new [b]customization and vanity options[/b] for characters and mounts, upgrades to [b]personal banks[/b], new [b]mobs[/b] and [b]skills[/b], expanded [b]Crystal GvGs and city scrims[/b], and much more. 

[img]https://i.imgur.com/OOdfAWN.png[/img]
[h1]Solo Randomized Dungeons are Coming[/h1]
The next step in Albion's open-world expansion is coming! Percival brings [b]Randomized Dungeons for solo players[/b], allowing you to explore on your own and face off against a host of fearsome new creatures. Like group dungeons, they will spawn at random throughout the world, allowing you to partake in thrilling solo dungeon-diving. You can also use rare dungeon maps to unlock [b]higher-tier solo dungeons[/b], which bring challenging foes and epic loot that increase in turn.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/AqndJqT.png[/img]
[h1]Customization and Vanity System + Bank Upgrades[/h1]
Percival brings a comprehensive new [b]customization and vanity system[/b] to the world of Albion, letting you show off your personality with dozens of hair, beard, face, and even underwear options. [b]Mount skins[/b] allow you to unlock permanent appearance-changing options for all characters on your account, and cover a large variety of both standard and exotic mounts. In addition to free options, you can also use gold to unlock [b]additional unique customization options[/b] to truly set your characters and mounts apart from the crowd!

[img]https://i.imgur.com/Cl8fd0q.png[/img]
[h1]New Mobs and Skills[/h1]
Along with Solo Randomized Dungeons, [b]new creatures[/b] have emerged from Albion's depths to face off against intrepid adventurers. These newly-designed mobs have a wide range of never-before-seen [b]spells and abilities[/b] at their disposal, requiring creative strategies and tactics to counter them. Fortunately for you, a variety of [b]new spells and abilities[/b] have been added to a diverse array of weapons, to make sure Albion's combat meta stays fresh and exciting, with new choices and unlocks for a huge range of combat builds.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/AWgGcxh.png[/img]
[h1]Additional Features and Improvements[/h1][list]	[*]New 20v20 city fight scrim option[/*]	[*]Crystal Realm Battles now available during the off season[/*]	[*]New Group Randomized Dungeon templates[/*]	[*]Separate language channels in chat[/*]	[*]Hotkeys for emotes[/*]	[*]...and more[/*][/list]
For a detailed list of everything coming with Percival, visit the [url=https://albiononline.com/en/update/Percival][b]update page[/b][/url].

[h1]Changes Coming for GvG Season 7[/h1]
And in addition to everything coming with Percival, some big changes to Albion's [b]GvG seasons[/b] are just around the corner. With the start of Season 7 right after the Percival launch, guild warfare will be updated and streamlined in regards to [b]GvG scheduling[/b], [b]castle claim times[/b], and many other core aspects of the system. We'll be announcing further details of these changes over the coming weeks, so stay tuned!

notes.title: Changelog: Oberon Patch 8
notes.notes:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/6680a76.jpg[/img]
[h1]Oberon Patch 8 - Ver. 1.14.381 / REV 143913 - 12 June 2019[/h1][h1]Vanity-Related Items Removed from Marketplace[/h1]
In anticipation of the new vanity / customization items coming with the Percival update, certain items, which will be converted to vanity items, [b]have had their sell orders canceled and can no longer be sold via the Marketplace[/b]. Since these items will likely be much more valuable in the future, this was done in order to protect players with long-running sell orders for these items from having them bought out from under them and resold (i.e. "flipped") by other players. These items are still tradable between players, but cannot be sold via the Marketplace after this update.

For the same reason, we have also canceled all sell orders for [b]Arena Sigils, Necromantic Elixirs, and Morgana Mare Saddles[/b]. These items will, however, remain tradable on the market, so that all owners have the chance to update their prices accordingly.

Due to the [b]Bonehorse [/b]and [b]Morgana Mare[/b] becoming permanent skins with the Percival update, we have reduced the drop chance of the corresponding mount upgrade items found in chests in Randomized Dungeons to 10% of its previous value.

We are no longer selling the guild-bannered [b]Warhorses [/b]in the Vanity Store. These items will return as vanity skins once Percival goes live. The current items can be used as before, and you will be able to exchange them for their original cost (Gold + Horse) when Percival goes live.

Finally, the time allowed to pick up items from unsold and canceled orders [b]has been increased to 60 days (formerly 30 days) for all items[/b].

For more information about this change, please see this forum post: [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/112754-Vanity-Customization/]https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/112754-Vanity-Customization/[/url]

[h1]Server Compensation[/h1]
This patch includes compensation items for those affected by recent latency issues. For further details, please see this article: [url=https://albiononline.com/en/news/fame-boost-and-premium-days]https://albiononline.com/en/news/fame-boost-and-premium-days[/url]

notes.title: Update on ongoing connection/latency issues resulting from DDOS
notes.notes:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/3p99Q0y.png[/img]

Dear Albion Community,

I'm here to update you on the state of the ongoing connection issues, the latency and sudden disconnects we're experiencing. Sadly, we have not yet found a solution, though it is not for a lack of trying. We've provided all information we have to our hosting partners and have been at their side the whole time, but so far we have no solution for the ongoing issues. 

From here we're doing three things:
[list]
[*] We'll continue to work on these issues with our current partners.
[*] We're looking into how to best compensate all players for the ongoing disruptions of gameplay. Any compensation will be announced and handed out AFTER the issues are resolved, however - since we want to ensure we find an appropriate compensation for the time period in which the problems persisted.
[*] We're actively looking into hosting alternatives and other partners to better deal with these problems in the future. The difficulty we're facing here is that many hosting companies are not too concerned with short term disruptions (as they typically deal with websites that can easily function with temporary connection issues), and fail to understand how crucial a continuous network connection is for a game service as ours. The other challenge here is that moving the entire infrastructure to a different partner is no simple feat and it has to be done carefully and correctly. Despite this, we've already found some potential partners, but this is more of a mid-term solution. That said, the work we’re putting in now will help us to be better prepared for similar attacks in the future.
[/list]
I will keep you posted and updated on further developments. We’re not satisfied until we can announce we’ve successfully dealt with this type of attack for good.

Sincerely,

Robin ‘Eltharyon’ Henkys
[i]Game Director[/i]

[h1]Oberon Patch 7 - Ver. 1.14.381 / REV 142821 - 22 May 2019[/h1]

[h1]Chest Loot Changes[/h1]
Chests in Randomized Dungeons are now loot-protected for the character or party that dealt the most damage to the last mob guarding the chest. Note that flagged characters who are hostile toward the character/party that killed the last mob can circumvent this loot protection and open the chest.

[h1]Invulnerability in Underway and Passageways[/h1]
The invulnerability bubble in the Underway and all other passageways now behaves as in other open-world zones (expires after 30 seconds or after moving 150 meters). Previously, these areas were classified as dungeons, meaning the buff would expire after 15 seconds or after moving 10 meters.

[b]Three major new Outland regions[/b] have been added to the world of Albion: [b]Siluria [/b](equivalent in size and value to Cumbria) and [b]West and East Glouvia[/b] (equivalent in size and value to West and East Anglia, respectively). While these regions will be claimable during the next Invasion Day (May 18), and will generate siphoned energy and spawn loot chests, they will not contribute season points to the current (sixth) GvG season. They will begin generating season points as normal at the beginning of Season 7.

In conjunction with this expansion and the redistribution of Outlands portals, [b]Energy Manipulator NPCs[/b] have been added close to the Realmgate in each of the Royal Cities.

For more on these changes and a list of portal/city connections for each region, click [url=https://albiononline.com/en/news/outland-expansion-incoming][b]here[/b][/url].

[h1]Portal Binding Reset[/h1]
Players can now remove their [b]portal binding[/b] (i.e. the lock to a particular city's Outlands portal) once every 30 days. This allows some flexibility with portal locks, while ensuring it only occurs for important reasons (guild moves, major strategic changes, urgent access to a new territory, etc.). The option of switching city bindings by traveling across the Outlands to a different-colored portal remains in effect.

[h1]Siege Camp Changes[/h1]
With the release of this update, the connections for the Siege Camps in [b]No Respite[/b] and [b]Carpet of Bones[/b] will be switched from Caerleon to [b]Martlock[/b] and [b]Thetford[/b], respectively. The newly introduced Siege Camps in [b]Desecrated Sands[/b], [b]Torn Earth[/b] and [b]Badbury Bog[/b] will be connected to the remaining Royal Cities. This change should make it significantly easier to compete for control of the Royal Cities.

[h1]Favorite Islands List[/h1]
By popular demand, players can now set certain islands as [b]favorites in the Travel Planner UI[/b], making them easily accessible without searching.

[h1]New Caerleon Marketplace Cluster[/h1]
To reduce overcrowding, a [b]second Marketplace cluster[/b] has been added to Caerleon, accessed by walking directly south from within the Bank of Caerleon. [b]Both clusters give access to the same Marketplace, including all for-sale items, buy orders, sell orders, and purchased goods[/b], and can be used interchangeably.
