notes.title: The Oberon Midseason Patch is Coming
notes.notes:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/FIL3UjG.jpg[/img]

Since Albion Online's free-to-play launch on April 10, the player base has grown tremendously, as new and veteran players alike set their sights on new regions and activities. To adjust for this massive influx of players, and to ensure that combat remains vital for all players, [b]Oberon Patch 5[/b] (AKA the [b]Oberon Midseason Patch[/b]) will bring a major new Outland expansion, portal binding and siege camp changes, the ability to set favorite islands, and more.

[h1]Outlands Expansion[/h1]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/aUZD0SZ.jpg[/img]

To give up-and-coming players (and smaller guilds both old and new) a chance at territory ownership, three major new Outland regions have been added: [b]Siluria [/b](equivalent in size and value to Cumbria), and [b]West and East Glouvia[/b] (equivalent in size and value to West and East Anglia, respectively). In the interest of fairness to teams currently competing in Season 6, these territories will be claimable beginning on the [b]second Invasion Day of Season 6[/b] (May 18), but [b]will not contribute season points until Season 7[/b].

[h1]Portal Binding and Siege Camp Updates[/h1]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/qNrvrhr.jpg[/img]

In conjunction with this expansion and the previous redistribution of Outlands portals to the Royal Cities, the following changes changes will take place:
[list]	[*]Players can now opt to remove their [b]portal binding[/b] once every 30 days. This long cooldown period allows for occasional cancellation of bindings due to unforeseen circumstances, while preventing unfettered access to all Outlands clusters. Players can still cross the Outlands to a different-colored portal in order to reset their bindings with no cooldown.[/*]	[*]To increase competition for control of the Royal Cities, the connections for the Siege Camps in [b]No Respite[/b] and [b]Carpet of Bones[/b] will be switched from Caerleon to [b]Martlock[/b] and [b]Thetford[/b], respectively. The newly introduced Siege Camps in [b]Desecrated Sands[/b], [b]Torn Earth[/b], and [b]Badbury Bog[/b] will enable attacks on the remaining Royal Cities.[/*]	[*]To further strengthen the connection between the Royal Cities and the Outlands, and for the convenience of all players, [b]Energy Manipulator NPCs[/b] have been added to the Royal Cities. These new merchants can be found near each city's Realmgate, and offer the same services that were previously available only in Caerleon.[/*][/list]
[h1]Favorite Islands List[/h1]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/6qDKSGA.jpg[/img]

By popular demand, players can now set certain islands as [b]favorites in the Travel Planner UI[/b]. This often-requested quality-of-life change allows players quick access to their most-visited islands without needing to search for them each time.

While this was one of the most-requested updates based on community feedback, the game's UI will also receive additional improvements and streamlining over the coming months - so please keep your feedback coming!

[h1]Combat Balance Changes[/h1]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/roja0De.jpg[/img]

The Oberon Midseason Patch brings numerous balance changes to weapons and armor. This set of changes has two specific goals in improving Albion's combat meta:
[list]	[*]Increasing the variety of tank builds in 5-versus-5 fights (GvGs, Hellgates, etc.)[/*]	[*]Bringing more variety in damage-dealing during ZvZs, and buffing some underutilized ZvZ weapons[/*][/list]
As always, the overarching goal of these changes is to keep combat in Albion fair and vital, and to keep builds for specific combat activities from becoming too stagnant and entrenched.

And speaking of combat, in case you missed it, you can now see every weapon, offhand, and tool in the game in one place - click [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/109516][b]here[/b][/url] to check it out.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/bUUsIhu.jpg[/img]

[b]Oberon [/b]is coming! The sixth major post-release content update for Albion Online brings [b]Randomized Dungeons[/b], new [b]creatures, chests and[/b] [b]shrines[/b], a completely reworked [b]tutorial[/b], numerous [b]quality-of-life improvements[/b], and much more. 

[h1]Hidden Entrances, Randomized Dungeons, and Dungeon Maps[/h1]
With Oberon, [b]Hidden Entrances[/b] will spawn randomly throughout the open world. These will not appear on maps, and must be discovered through exploration. Within these entrances are [b]Randomized Dungeons[/b]: one-of-a-kind, procedurally generated lairs that offer a new gameplay experience each time, with the potential to contain rare bosses and valuable loot. Players can also use [b]Dungeon Maps[/b], a new item dropped by mobs, to show the locations of nearby dungeons.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/AlSraHZ.png[/img]

[h1]New Creatures, Loot Drops, Shrines, and Chests[/h1]
Oberon brings a host of [b]ferocious new foes[/b], from ethereal wisps and devious Acolytes to the fiendish Keeper Witch. Roaming mobs throughout the open world now drop [b]runes, souls, and relics[/b], bringing new economic and crafting possibilities. [b]Chests[/b] have been reworked with updated visuals, and are now sealed with a magical shield that can only be broken by killing nearby mobs. And new [b]shrines[/b] can be found in Randomized Dungeons, offering brief but powerful whole-party buffs.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/JfqUDzl.png[/img]

[h1]Reworked Tutorial, Quicker Combat Unlocks, and Quality-of-Life Improvements[/h1]
An all-new [b]tutorial[/b] gives new players clearer guidance on the game's systems and combat. This will bring them more quickly into higher-level play, benefitting new and veteran players alike. The [b]early-tier grind[/b] to unlock weapons, armor, and gathering gear has been reduced, encouraging players to experiment with new builds and playstyles. Oberon also brings long-requested improvements to [b]crafting and transmutation[/b] times, plus [b]reduced harvest times for creature resources[/b]. Additionally, players can now mute up to 150 others, limits have been placed on excessive whispers to reduce in-game spam, and the toolbars and ingame shop are clearer and easier to navigate.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/3ekinKs.png[/img]

For a detailed list of everything coming with Oberon, visit the [url=https://albiononline.com/en/update/Oberon][b]update page[/b][/url].

notes.title: The Nimue Balance Patch is Live
notes.notes:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/lqsIuol.png[/img]

Nimue Patch 7, AKA the [b]Nimue Balance Patch[/b], is here. While the patch includes a broad range of updates and fixes to weapons and armor, the most noteworthy changes are those to [b]overall Hitpoints, Energy, and Movement Speed[/b]:
[list]	[*]The Hitpoint pool has been increased by 20% across the board to increase the time needed to kill an enemy. Along with other adjustments, this should prevent one-shot builds.[/*]	[*]To complement the higher Hitpoint pool, the overall Energy pool has also been raised by 20%.[/*]	[*]Movement speed has also been increased, which will make combat more fluid. It will also allow faster travel across zones, improving the overall game feel.[/*][/list]
We've made a couple of ability reworks to further increase the variety in builds: swords can temporarily become purge immune, Fire Staffs have a zoning tool on the Q slot, and the Guardian Helmet now can remove DoTs, for example.

In general, we are looking forward to a new and exciting meta and are excited to see what builds you will come up with. The complete patch notes can be found below, as well as on our [url=https://albiononline.com/en/update][b]Updates page[/b][/url].

[img]https://i.imgur.com/w2RjI72.png[/img]

notes.title: Dev Update: Hidden Entrances and Randomized Dungeons
notes.notes:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/NSCasZi.gif[/img]

In a recent [url=https://albiononline.com/en/news/devtalk-nimue-development-update][b]Dev Talk[/b][/url], Game Director Robin Henkys gave a brief rundown of some of the new features coming to Albion in 2019. Two major new features, [b]Hidden Entrances[/b] and [b]Randomized Dungeons[/b], will be introduced with the Oberon update this spring. 

[h1][b]What are Hidden Entrances and Randomized Dungeons?[/b][/h1]
[b]Hidden Entrances[/b] are gateways that spawn at random throughout the open world, in all zones and at all times. Their frequency is such that a party of five should be able to find an entrance readily enough. Though their location is not revealed on the minimap, they are accessible to all players for as long as they remain open, meaning multiple parties can enter at one time.

Within these discoverable portals are [b]Randomized Dungeons[/b]. These dungeons are created procedurally based on numerous parameters, influencing everything from mob type to room and corridor layout to bosses and loot.

Each dungeon will only last for a limited time, and will begin to lose stability the longer it remains open. The transitive nature of these dungeons provides an incentive to move through them quickly - not only to claim the loot within, but also to avoid being transported back to the overworld along with any hostile players within.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/WMHn55Y.jpg[/img]

[h1][b]What are the goals of these features?[/b][/h1]
These features bring an entirely new source of open-world PvE to the world of Albion. The unpredictable nature of both Hidden Entrances and the Randomized Dungeons they conceal makes them a much more varied experience than anything previously seen in the game, falling somewhere between the safe fame-farming of Expeditions and the high-risk PvP of static dungeons. The dungeons introduced with the Oberon update will be for a five-person group, but soloable dungeons and other types of content will be introduced with later updates.

While Randomized Dungeons, at launch, will mostly feature known factions and mobs, these will be reworked and optimized, and some new enemies will be introduced to the game as well. In the long run, the combination of Hidden Entrances and Randomized Dungeons will give us a platform for introducing entirely new types of PvE content into the game, including entirely new mobs, dungeons, and experiences.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/9aIiINO.jpg[/img]

[b]Here's a quick rundown on the current state of Hidden Entrances and Randomized Dungeons:[/b]
[list]	[*]Both features are already working code-wise (randomized generation of dungeon layouts and placement of Hidden Entrances in the world)[/*]	[*]Game design is currently balancing mobs and loot levels to provide a rewarding player experience[/*]	[*]Level design and art are creating the necessary connectors and highlights for each dungeon type[/*]	[*]Heretic and Morgana dungeons are finished, and Keeper dungeons are underway[/*]	[*]Game design and QA are performing regular internal playtests to iterate on dungeon progress[/*][/list]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/LywxGCX.jpg[/img]

We'll have much more info on these features in our forthcoming series of Dev Talks, so stay tuned!

notes.title: Patch 6 Brings Crafting Bonuses, Spell Fixes, and More
notes.notes:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/ZDwTafK.jpg[/img]

Nimue Patch 6 launched today, bringing several important economic updates along with audio upgrades and an assortment of combat and spell changes.

Most significant among the changes are the [b]higher travel cost modifier of certain laborer journals[/b] and the [b]increased local refining efficiency bonuses[/b] of the Royal Cities. These changes bring the time and risk involved in transporting goods more in line with the rewards, and, conversely, offer greater rewards to those willing to put in the time to transport goods.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/1TIZmxP.jpg[/img]

For full details of Nimue Patch 6, see below.

[h1]Nimue Patch #6 - Ver. 1.13.369 / REV 134359 - 28 January 2019[/h1]

[h1]Improvements[/h1][list]	[*][b]Royal Armor[/b] can now be enchanted with the corresponding Runes, Souls, and Relics[/*]	[*]Further improved [b]Arena matchmaking[/b] to more equally balance skill levels between teams[/*]	[*][b]GvG and Crystal Realm match result notifications[/b] changed from pop-up windows to white text to avoid hindering gameplay[/*]	[*][b]Audio improvements:[/b]	[list]		[*]Redesigned Holy and Nature Staff auto-attack and impact sounds[/*]		[*]Reworked sounds for Direboar, Moabird, and Impala mounts[/*]		[*]Added idle sounds to Alchemist[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*][b]Animation improvements:[/b]	[list]		[*]Updated effects for Fire Aura and Razor Cut[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list][h1]Changes[/h1][list]	[*][b]Fast travel costs[/b] have been increased for laborer journals used to produce resources or refined resources	[list]		[*]The cost is now roughly the same as it would be to transport the corresponding resources (calculated at 100% laborer happiness) directly[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*][b]Local refining efficiency bonuses in Royal Cities[/b] have been raised to make transporting materials to these cities more worthwhile. notes.title: The Nimue Update Arrives November 21!
notes.notes:
[b]Nimue[/b] is coming! The fifth major post-release content update for Albion Online arrives November 21, bringing several major new features, numerous quality-of-life improvements, and various updates to creatures, combat, and the open-world experience.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/kY4fSFD.jpg[/img]
[h1]Crystal Realm Battles[/h1]
Enter the Crystal Realm and face off against other guilds in full-loot, 5v5 battles over valuable rewards and energy. With a huge number of daily battles and all participants receiving a proportional share of the loot, this system gives new GvG teams a chance at the spoils of guild warfare. It all takes place in the Crystal Realm, a new arena featuring a gorgeous art style imbued with light and color.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/xN5j6BX.jpg[/img]
[h1]Party Finder, Guild Logo Updates, and Quality-of-Life Improvements[/h1]
The [b]Party Finder[/b] is an all-new lobby system that allows solo players, small groups, and guilds to create and join parties and participate in a broad range of open-world activities. And in addition to the ability to preview [b]guild logos[/b] in various contexts and change them after creation, Nimue also brings numerous other [b]quality-of-life improvements[/b], including:
[list]	[*]Prearranged parties remain after Arena / Expedition end[/*]	[*]Keyboard shortcut to move items without stacking[/*]	[*]Gear locking in duels[/*]	[*]Guild account logs for Silver and Gold transactions[/*][/list]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/mjKnEnD.jpg[/img]
[h1]New Creatures and Accessories[/h1]
[b]Guardian Aspects[/b] are smaller versions of the current Raid Guardians, which spawn randomly in the open world and offer an opportunity for smaller groups to earn valuable resources. And the five new [b]Mob Faction capes[/b] (created with special crests dropped by elite mobs) complement diverse combat builds with unique passive spells such as:
[list]	[*][b]Undead Cape[/b]: Invisibility (Escape / Utility)[/*]	[*][b]Keeper Cape[/b]: Damage Increase (Bruiser / Tank)[/*]	[*][b]Demon Cape[/b]: Lava Pool (DPS)[/*][/list]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/mPqoMrC.jpg[/img]
[h1]Other Additions and Changes[/h1][list]	[*][b]Reworked Farming and Furniture Placement[/b] - Farming and furniture placement have been streamlined, allowing you to place crops, herbs, animals, and furniture at the mouse cursor's position.[/*]	[*][b]Improved NPCs and City Buildings[/b] - Numerous merchants and craftspeople have new character models, animation, and voiceovers, and city buildings have new lighting effects for improved nighttime visibility[/*]	[*][b]Arena and Faction Outpost Improvements[/b] - These systems have been reworked to improve queuing and small-group experiences.[/*]	[*][b]Additional Improvements[/b] - Nimue also brings Outlands resource rebalancing, numerous bug fixes and combat balancing updates, visual improvements throughout the open world, and much more.[/*][/list]
For a detailed list of everything coming with Nimue, visit the [url=https://albiononline.com/en/update/Nimue][b]update page[/b][/url].

notes.title: Albion Online Dev Talk - Nimue Development Update
notes.notes:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/GcjQWFs.jpg[/img]

The next major content update for Albion Online, [b]Nimue[/b], is coming soon. In this Dev Talk, Robin Henkys discusses some of the major changes and new features this update will bring.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EiQ3B-44kSU
Don't have time to watch the video? Read on for a written summary of his talk. For more context you can also read the full details of the current Albion Online Development Roadmap in [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/97535-Development-Roadmap-beyond-Merlyn/][b]this forum post[/b][/url].

[h1]Recent Changes[/h1]
In the last couple of weeks we’ve already delivered some of the new content, rewards and improvements promised in the roadmap:
[list]	[*]Adventurer’s Challenges[/*]	[*]Guild Warfare Season Rewards[/*]	[*]The return of season points for mage killing[/*]	[*]Limits on guild hopping[/*][/list]
So what can you expect next?

[h1]Nimue: Quality of Life, Crystal Realm Battles, Party Finder, and Season Updates[/h1]
Next up is the release of the [b]Nimue[/b] content update in late November. (If you're wondering, it's named after the mythical “Lady of the Lake” in Arthurian legend.)

Nimue will be an opportunity to roll out a long list of quality of life improvements you’ve been asking for. This includes:
[list]	[*]The ability to change your guild logo after guild creation and to preview your guild logo in a variety of different contexts[/*]	[*]The ability to mark a player or NPC as a target in battle[/*]	[*]The ability to see your party members' combat roles (tank, healer, damage dealer, etc.) while in the open world[/*]	[*]And many other changes[/*][/list]
In addition, Nimue will be an opportunity to roll out two major features from our roadmap:

[h1]Crystal Realm Battles[/h1]
Crystal Realm Battles provide a daily opportunity to enter the magical Crystal plane and fight other guilds attempting to do the same thing in a GvG-style battle. Of all the features in Nimue, we’re most excited about this one, as it will significantly increase the number of GvG battles to well over a hundred battles every day, opening lots of opportunities for new GvG teams to make a name for themselves.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/HlvJ2eK.jpg[/img]

[h1]Party Finder[/h1]
The second is the Party Finder, which is a lobby-style system that allows players to publicly post and join activities. This should make finding parties for all activities in Albion significantly easier, as well as serve as a tool for organizing activities within guilds.

Both these features as well as the other changes coming with Nimue will be the subject of upcoming dev talk videos.

Finally, of course, you can also expect Adventurer’s Challenges to continue - and we’re already thinking about what rewards and changes there will be for GvG Season 5!

[h1]Beyond Nimue: Random Dungeons vs. Hardcore Expeditions[/h1]
We’re already deep in development for some larger features beyond Nimue, the biggest of which are random dungeon entrances. This brand-new feature will be nothing short of a redefinition of open-world PvE in Albion Online.

Here's what the feature entails:
[list]	[*]Not just the location of the dungeon, but the structure of the dungeon itself will be randomized and unpredictable[/*]	[*]Dungeons will be generated dynamically when the first player enters, the mobs in them will not respawn, and the dungeons will collapse after being cleared[/*]	[*]This will enable a roaming style of group PvE, where you look for dungeon entrances in the open world and you actually explore an entire dungeon before starting the next[/*]	[*]Due to the unpredictable placement of the entrances, these dungeons will be significantly more safe from PvP, since gankers will have to scout the entrances first[/*]	[*]In terms of risk vs. reward, we aim to make them a far better PvE activity than hardcore expeditions[/*][/list]
Since this change will have such a big impact on Albion, we’re taking our time to get it just right.

That said, we’re making good progress and we’ll keep you posted as development continues.

That's all for today - we hope this talk gives you a good idea of what we’ve been working on, what you can expect to see in the Nimue update, and a little preview of what to expect beyond.

We'll be bringing you more Dev Talks soon, where we’ll get up close and personal with Crystal Realm Battles, the new Party Finder system, and the many quality of life improvements coming with the Nimue update. Thanks for watching!

[img]https://i.imgur.com/WmodMWc.jpg[/img]

[h1][b]Merlyn Season 4 Patch - Ver. 1.12.365 / REV 127503 - 10 October 2018[/b][/h1]

Fall is in the air, and Halloween is coming! [b]Halloween decorations[/b] have returned to all of Albion's cities.

[h1][b]Guild and Alliance Cooldowns[/b][/h1]
Based on community feedback, the following cooldowns now apply:
[list]	[*]After [b]joining [/b]a guild, you may not join another guild for [b]48 hours[/b].[/*]	[*]After [b]joining [/b]an alliance, your guild may not join another alliance for [b]48 hours[/b].[/*]	[*][b]LEAVING[/b] a guild or alliance does not trigger any cooldown period.[/*][/list]
This change has been introduced during the early phases of Season 4 to shake up GvG combat, keep the season interesting, and put smaller and newer guilds on more even footing with larger and more established ones.

[h1][b]Siphoning Mages and Season Points[/b][/h1]
Additionally, also based on community feedback, killing [b]Siphoning Mages[/b] will now [b]once again yield season points[/b]. In order to prevent exploits, this means that we're also removing the ability to place Siphoning and Rogue Mages for energy. This change should serve to keep the current season vital, while also leaving the possibility open that mages will be further updated or replaced with a new system in future seasons.

[h1][b]Warhorses[/b][/h1]
[b]Warhorses [/b]are a new item available from the Vanity Merchant in major cities. These mount overlays can be combined with any T5-T8 Armored Horse to create a visual upgrade that keeps the stats of the original mount while prominently displaying the owner's guild logo.

[h1][b]Combat Balance Changes[/b][/h1][list]	[*][b]Fatal Blade (Black Monk Staff)[/b]	[list]		[*]Cooldown now scales with item power. (Example values: 1200IP → 18s / 1700 IP → 16s)[/*]		[*]Slow now always lasts the intended 6s, and no longer scales with ability power[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]

notes.title: Season 4 Patch Brings Essential Guild Updates
notes.notes:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/MTasStR.jpg[/img]

With the fourth Guild Warfare Season [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/97122-GvG-Season-4-Schedule/][b]already underway[/b][/url], GvG warfare has once again come to the world of Albion. The Season 4 Patch, coming October 10, will bring an important change that has long been requested by the Albion Online community: [b]limits on guild- and alliance-hopping[/b].

[h1][b]Guild and Alliance Cooldowns[/b][/h1]
After maintenance on the 10th, the following rules will apply:
[list]	[*]After [b]joining [/b]a guild, you cannot join another guild for [b]48 hours[/b].[/*]	[*]After [b]joining [/b]an alliance, your guild cannot join another alliance for [b]48 hours[/b].[/*]	[*][b]LEAVING[/b] a guild or alliance does not trigger any cooldown period.[/*][/list]
We've received a great deal of feedback on this issue, with the general sentiment that the ability to jump from guild to guild with no penalty helps larger guilds maintain their holds on territories and contributes to stagnation of GvG seasons by maintaining the status quo. As such, we're introducing it during this early phase of Season 4 to shake up GvG combat, keep the season interesting, and put smaller and newer guilds on more even footing with larger and more established ones.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/UA7AsZQ.png[/img]

[h1][b]Siphoning Mage Changes[/b][/h1]
Additionally, based on community feedback, killing Siphoning Mages will now once again yield season points. In order to prevent exploits, this means that we're also removing the ability to place mages for energy. This change should open up the possibility for players to contribute to their guild's season success outside of GvGs and reset days.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/IiR3obA.jpg[/img]

[h1][b]Warhorses, New Choke Points, and More[/b][/h1]
Also coming with this patch are [b]Warhorses[/b], a new item available from the Vanity Merchant in major cities. These mount overlays can be combined with any T5-T8 Armored Horse to create a Warhorse, which keeps the stats of the original mount while prominently displaying the owner's guild logo. Warhorses are perfect for large-scale guild battles, allowing you to stay visible to fellow guild members, rally fellow alliance members, or intimidate your foes – and look good doing it.

Based on community feedback, we've also updated numerous open-world maps to include more [b]choke points[/b], which allow for a broader range of combat options. Whether you're an attacker or a defender, make sure you're aware of these lower-mobility spots and use them to your advantage!

All the details of the Season 4 Patch will be published soon in the [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Board/78-Feedback-Testserver/][b]Feedback Testserver[/b][/url] forum.

notes.notes:

[h1][b]Merlyn Preseason Balance Patch - Ver. 1.12.365 / REV 126590 - 26 September 2018[/b][/h1]

[h1][b]GvG Season Rewards[/b][/h1]
Beginning with Season 4, GvG Seasons in Albion Online will include epic rewards for reaching various ranks. Players who are part of an eligible guild for at least 75% of the season will win the powerful new [b]War Rhino[/b] mount (Bronze rank or higher) and [b]exclusive avatars and avatar rings[/b] (Iron rank or higher). Additionally, the top three guilds each season will get a permanent place in the new [b]Conquerors' Hall[/b], a new building in Caerleon that will honor past and current winners with custom-built statues and will expand with each successive GvG season.

For more details on the new season rewards, click [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/97187-GvG-Season-Rewards-Conquerors-Hall-F-A-Q/][b]here[/b][/url].  For a calendar with all the important Season 4 dates, click [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/97122-GvG-Season-4-Schedule/][b]here[/b][/url].

[h1][b]Monthly Adventurer's Challenges[/b][/h1]
Starting October 1, all players in Albion can partake in monthly [b]Adventurer's Challenges[/b] to get exclusive mounts, special potions and treasures, and numerous other rewards. Each month will have a different theme, and rewards will often include seasonal and thematic items.

Rewards are given out for acquiring [b]gathering, fishing, and PvE Fame[/b], with daily bonuses that boost your points even higher – for more details on Adventurer's Challenges, click [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/97493-Adventurers-Challenge-FAQ/][b]here[/b][/url].

Updated Marketplace, management, and map UIs:

[b]Trade Missions[/b]

To reconcile the risk of Faction Trade Missions with their rewards, the weight of the Medium Trade Mission quest item "Unsuspicious Boxes" was increased from 288.5kg to 688kg. Transporting this item will now generally require mounts with higher load capacity (such as regular horses, stags, and oxen) and exclude many mounts with higher survivability. This increases the risk of these lucrative missions, and brings them more in line with the current rewards.

[list][*]Fixed an issue where custom match invitations sent during GvG battles (and the resulting auto-cancellation notices) were interfering with gameplay
[*]Fixed an issue where players were unable to enter names for new guild roles
[*]Fixed an issue where an Expedition would not complete when the final boss was killed after a player respawned
[*]Fixed an issue where characters affected by Fear sometimes ran back into Wall of Flames
[*]Fixed an issue where Hellgate names did not appear correctly in death details
[*]Additional graphical, UI, and localization fixes
[/list]

notes.title: Changelog: Lancelot Patch #8
notes.notes:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/WmodMWc.jpg[/img]

[h1]Lancelot Patch #8 - Ver. 1.11.362 / REV 118917 - 6 June 2018[/h1]

[b]Changes[/b]
[list]
[*]Numerous Destiny Board issues have been tackled:
[*]Added specialization nodes for crafting of Bags, Capes, and Demolition Hammers
[*]Having a complete specialization now gives the same amount of focus cost reduction and an increased chance for higher-quality crafting events as crafting similar items
[*]Basic tool crafting node now offers a higher boost to the crafting of all corresponding items
[*]Non-artifact offhand specialization node now offers a higher boost to the crafting of all corresponding offhand items
[*]Offhand combat specializations now offer the same amount of item power when maxed out as other weapon specializations: for example, with T8 dual daggers, average item power is 1360; with T8 one-handed dagger + torch, average item power is now also 1360. (Previously, offhand items granted 40 less item power when maxed out.)
[*]The goal of these changes was to make sure that all items (besides consumables) will have the same degree of bonuses if all nodes have been completely mastered. Of course, the relative amount of fame to achieve this condition will be related to the overall importance of the item.
[*]Mastery level crafting requirements for Bags, Capes, and Demolition Hammers have been updated as follows:
[*]T4: 1 → 1 (unchanged)
[*]T5: 20 → 10
[*]T6: 43 → 30
[*]T7: 64 → 60
[*]T8: 76 → 100
[*]Relic armors have now been added to the overall loot tables, meaning the Black Market will now buy these items and redistribute them to open-world mobs.
[/list]

[b]Fixes[/b]
[list]
[*]Dash can now be interrupted by stun and ground effects 
[*]Farming achievements now correctly display the actual Fame needed
[*]Fixed an issue where an unlocalized error message would display while rerolling quality of an item
[*]Fixed an issue where the buff during Deflecting Spin would cancel for no reason
[*]Fixed an issue where Wanderlust buff sometimes dropped while stacking up
[*](iOS) Fixed an issue where audio would drop out unpredictably
[*](LINUX) Ubuntu 18 is now supported
[*]Numerous additional graphical, texture, audio, animation, UI, and localization fixes
